name: Aranmula Kannadi
tagline: World‑famous hand‑polished bimetal mirror from Aranmula
summary: A rare, first‑surface metal mirror handmade in Aranmula village. Crafted by a few Vishwakarma families using a secret copper‑tin alloy and intensive hand polishing, it is an iconic Kerala craft with…
description: Aranmula Kannadi is a hand‑made metal alloy mirror made in the temple village of Aranmula in Pathanamthitta district. Unlike glass mirrors, its image reflects from the mirror’s front surface; the alloy recipe and finishing techniques remain closely held by traditional maker families.

The mirror matters as living heritage: it links local temple ritual, artisanal metallurgy and Kerala gift culture. Aranmula mirrors appear in Ashtamangalyam temple offerings, are prized wedding and house‑warming gifts, and feature in museum shows of Asian metalwork.

Visitors find a craft practised by a few master families, slow casting and many days of hand polishing, and a range of traditional shapes from small pocket mirrors to ornate wall Valkannadi. Buying from authorised makers supports the families who keep the technique alive.
highlights: Only metal, first‑surface mirror made in Aranmula village
Traditional know‑how held by a few Vishwakarma/metal‑smith families
Geographical Indication (GI) protected (registered and managed by local society)
Laborious hand‑polishing for clear surface reflection
Associated with Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple and ritual gift culture

sections.heading: Background
body: Aranmula Kannadi is a traditional metal mirror that local tradition links to the Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple and to a small number of artisan families in the village. The craft is centuries old in local memory and is described in museum and tourism literature as unique to Aranmula.

The mirrors are made from a special copper‑tin alloy; makers guard the exact formula and finishing process as family knowledge. The product has Geographical Indication (GI) protection registered to the Viswabrahmana Aranmula Kannadi Nirman Society, with documents and renewal records held by the GI Registry.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: See artisans at work in small workshops and handicraft stalls in and around Aranmula village; watch the finishing and polishing stages (many steps are manual and require patience). Look for classic Valkannadi wall mirrors and smaller hand mirrors.

Shop from recognised makers and authorised outlets in Aranmula or government emporiums; genuine mirrors are hand‑made, can take weeks of finishing and usually carry GI details or authorised‑maker information. Ask about provenance — the craft is closely connected to named families and local workshops.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Aranmula is a heritage temple village on the banks of the Pamba River; combine a craft visit with the Parthasarathy Temple and the riverside. Workshops are small — plan visits by appointment and buy directly from makers if possible.

When buying, confirm maker details and GI/authenticity information. Respect workshop etiquette: ask before photographing, do not pressure artisans to reveal secret formulas, and expect handcrafted pieces to cost more and take time compared with mass‑produced mirrors.

latest.text: A legal appeal by the Thikkinampallil Aranmula Metal Mirror Nirman Family Charitable Trust against the GI office order was dismissed by the Madras High Court for non‑prosecution on 5 Nov 2024 (case document available online).

Rijksmuseum (Amsterdam) staged the exhibition 'Asian Bronze: 4,000 Years of Beauty' (27 Sep 2024–12 Jan 2025); museum exhibitions on Asian bronze highlighted historic and living metal techniques. Local artisans reported an Aranmula mirror was shown as part of this international display.

GI Registry records show renewal action/filing activity for the Aranmula Kannadi Geographical Indication on 10 Apr 2023; the GI certificate and related producer details are published on the IP India site.

visitorInfo.howToReach: Aranmula lies on the Pamba river in Pathanamthitta. Nearest railhead: Chengannur (about 10–12 km). Nearest major airport: Thiruvananthapuram/Trivandrum (roughly 116–120 km). Regular road connections, taxis and buses link Aranmula with nearby towns.
etiquette: Buy only from recognised makers or authorised emporiums and ask for GI/producer details — confirm before you travel when you need a specific size or finish.
Workshops are family run; ask permission before photographing and do not demand disclosure of secret alloy/formula.
Be prepared for handmade lead times — some mirrors need days or weeks of finishing; guarantee authenticity rather than low price.
If you want a workshop visit, call ahead and arrange an appointment; many makers welcome respectful visitors but operate small workshops.
